title: Missing cost rows produce PARTIAL coverage instead of a cheaper cost per outcome
risk: Rows with no cost are dropped from the cost numerator, so cost per successful outcome falls whenever a billing feed breaks and the platform looks cheaper exactly when it is unmeasured.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
kpi_edge.missing_cost marks two rows whose cost is absent because the provider feed did not deliver, which is different from a cost of zero.
Cost per successful outcome must state its coverage when any contributing row has no cost.

steps.action: Compute cost per successful outcome over the full window
steps.expected: The value is 30 TWD and the report states that two contributing rows have no cost, so the figure is marked PARTIAL rather than final.

steps.action: Attempt to publish the figure as complete
steps.expected: Publication is refused while a contributing row lacks cost; the missing rows are listed with the provider-feed reason.

steps.action: Attempt to treat the missing cost as zero
steps.expected: The substitution is refused, because a zero would silently lower the measured cost per outcome.

steps.action: Aggregate cost per run and per customer after the feed recovers
steps.expected: The restated figure includes the previously missing rows, per-customer cost sums to the run totals, and the earlier PARTIAL state is superseded by a recorded restatement.

assertions: Cost per successful outcome is never published as complete while any contributing row lacks a cost; the coverage state is PARTIAL with the reason.
A missing cost is never replaced by zero, and the recomputation before and after the feed recovery differ only by the recovered amounts.
Per-run and per-customer cost aggregates reconcile to the measured total, with no cost attributed to a customer that did not generate it.
The restatement is recorded with its cause, so the previously published partial figure can still be reconstructed.
forbidden: Substituting zero for a missing provider cost.
Dropping the rows without cost from the numerator so the average falls.
Publishing a per-customer cost that cannot be reconciled to the run totals.
evidence: Cost computation with the PARTIAL coverage state and the missing row ids.
Provider usage and billing extract showing which rows are absent.
Restatement record created after the feed recovery.
cleanup: Delete gov- cost aggregate rows and invented cost rows after export; the provider feed substitute is restored.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
prerequisites: ASM-002 is unlocked, so the cost figures are measurements with unapproved thresholds; only the coverage and reconciliation rules are asserted here.
